from the U.S. Department of Energy's SPARK program to support its Montour grid modernization project of an existing 230-kV transmission corridor.

The proposed Montour Grid Resilience and Advanced Reconductoring Project will rebuild 29.3 miles of existing transmission line, strengthening reliability and enhancing the line's available capacity while maximizing the use of existing infrastructure, benefiting customers throughout the Susquehanna Valley, Greater Lehigh Valley, and Northeast Pennsylvania.

said the project will deploy two advanced transmission technologies supported through the DoE's SPARK program: the use of a combination of Aluminum Conductor Steel Supported and Aluminum Conductor Composite Core conductors which can carry more electricity, improve performance during high temperatures, and provide greater long-term reliability; and the installation of dual optical ground wire to strengthen system protection and communications while expanding the corridor's fiber network.

"Today's announcement reinforces the Trump administration's commitment to common-sense energy addition policies that lower electricity prices and strengthen our grid," U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said.

title: PPL selected for up to $71.5M DoE grant for Pennsylvania transmission upgrade
